newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spanish fishermen slam EU-Morocco squid haul rules.
newsitem.headline: Spanish fishermen slam EU-Morocco squid haul rules.

text.p: Angry Spanish fishermen demanded compensation on Thursday following a European Commission decision to extend fishing restrictions in Moroccan waters.

"This decision only serves to further ruin a sector which is being maltreated by the various administrations and we still have not seen the help that we were promised," Ismael Galloso, chairman of the Punta Umbria Shipowners' Association, said.

Spain's agriculture ministry said on Thursday the European Commission, the European Union's executive body, had agreed to extend a two-month fishing ban on what it termed over-exploited cephalopods, including octopus, squid and cuttlefish, and associated species, to give stocks time to develop.
Cephalopod fishing now will be illegal in the months of March and April as well as September and October as laid down in an EU-Morocco fisheries accord reached last year.
Fishing groups representing about 110 Spanish boats affected by the decision demanded financial aid from the EU and Spain to alleviate losses due to the ban.

"I'm sure Morocco had best of intentions but I hope the Spanish administration introduces the correct measures to aid the fishermen during this period," Jose Ramon Fontan from another shipowners' association said.
The agriculture ministry said it was studying the EU agreement and the possibility of giving aid to fishermen, but it has yet to make a decision.
Spain's heavy use of Moroccan waters was a sore point in diplomatic relations between the two countries last year during EU-Moroccan talks on renewing the fishing licence.

After months of wrangling Morocco finally reached a four-year fisheries agreement under which the EU pays the North African country $162.5 million a year in fees for fishing rights for the mainly Spanish fleet.
The accord allows 600 fishing boats from southern Spain, the Canary Islands and Portugal to operate in Moroccan waters.
